summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca), signed the node's ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with principals node1/NODE_IP/localhost, and configured sshd (HostCertificate directive in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-host-cert.conf) to present it. Verified a client trusting only the CA (via a known_hosts @cert-authority line, no pinned host key) connects successfully (host verification passes; only publickey auth fails as expected). Enabled and started the previously-disabled ssh service. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now`, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified ssh service active/enabled, cert files intact, and CA-based client trust still works post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 SSH state (no host keys existed yet, ssh service inactive/disabled)
Created a dedicated ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca
Signed the host's ed25519 public key into a host certificate valid for node1/NODE_IP/localhost, forever
Added HostCertificate directive to sshd_config.d and validated config with sshd -t
Verified end-to-end that a client trusting only the CA public key connects without host-key pinning
Captured baseline boot_id and health, rebooted node1, polled until back online, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified ssh service, certificate files, and CA-based client trust after restart
